anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address-select pin A0 (U2 pin 1) is tied to the +3.3V rail, while A1 to A5 (U2 pins 2 to 5 and 24) are all tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: With A0 to A5 all low, the PCA9685 responds at its default address 0x40, as the specification states. Tying A0 high gives 0x41.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The FCC firmware addressing the servo driver at 0x40 would get no response, so the PWM outputs to the servos would not be driven. The INA219 (U1) has A0 and A1 both on GND, consistent with its specified 0x40.

anomalies.observed: All five VDD pins and the VDDA pin of the FCC STM32H753 are on isolated unconnected nets. The +3V3 rail, which carries the MCU decoupling, has no connection to any FCC1 supply pin.
anomalies.expected: The STM32 digital supply pins and VDDA must be connected to the 3V3 rail, as the specification states that 3V3 feeds both MCUs.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: If real, the FCC would have no supply and would not run. This is more likely a netlist-level wiring gap than a board-level fault, so it is a lower-confidence finding.
